k: The Ardent says it's just a story. The Ardent gave our stone away. I'm old. I notice things.
src: 'The Ardent says it\'s just a story. The Ardent gave our stone away. I\'m old. I notice things.'

k: You went down beneath the isle for us. Even though you think the Hierophant is wrong.
src: 'You went down beneath the isle for us. Even though you think the Hierophant is wrong.'

k: I don't know what to do with that. I have been praying about it. The wind has not answered.
src: 'I don\'t know what to do with that. I have been praying about it. The wind has not answered.'

k: When the Vespersong is sung, no one will ever be lost to the storm again. No more empty chairs at supper.
src: 'When the Vespersong is sung, no one will ever be lost to the storm again. No more empty chairs at supper.'

k: Don't you want that? Doesn't everyone want that?
src: 'Don\'t you want that? Doesn\'t everyone want that?'

k: Ilka's put Skyreach-cut lift-crystals in that old tub. She'll climb like a lark now.
src: 'Ilka\'s put Skyreach-cut lift-crystals in that old tub. She\'ll climb like a lark now.'

k: Your captain flew her up through the Stormcrown on _desert glass_. Nobody up here will ever buy him a drink again — they'll be too busy telling the story.
src: 'Your captain flew her up through the Stormcrown on _desert glass_. Nobody up here will ever buy him a drink again — they\'ll be too busy telling the story.'

k: I saw you come up through the storm. Thought you were a falling barn.
src: 'I saw you come up through the storm. Thought you were a falling barn.'

k: Then I thought: no, a barn would fly better.
src: 'Then I thought: no, a barn would fly better.'

k: The Lord-Commander came on a black warship, three weeks back. The Ardent handed him our stone on the steps of the Lantern, and everybody cheered.
src: 'The Lord-Commander came on a black warship, three weeks back. The Ardent handed him our stone on the steps of the Lantern, and everybody cheered.'

k: I cheered. Loudest of anyone.
src: 'I cheered. Loudest of anyone.'

k: ...I don't know why I cheered.
src: '...I don\'t know why I cheered.'

k: Depart
src: 'Depart'

k: A fountain fed by rain-catchers. Coins glint at the bottom: offerings to the wind, for safe flights. There are a great many coins.
src: 'A fountain fed by rain-catchers. Coins glint at the bottom: offerings to the wind, for safe flights. There are a great many coins.'

k: The Halcyon, nose-down in what used to be Ilka's shed. One mast is broken. The other is somehow holding a chicken.
src: 'The Halcyon, nose-down in what used to be Ilka\'s shed. One mast is broken. The other is somehow holding a chicken.'

k: Ilka's yard. Where the Halcyon crashed, there is a neat pile of salvaged timber labeled, in large letters, CORVIN'S. YOU'RE PAYING FOR THIS.
src: 'Ilka\'s yard. Where the Halcyon crashed, there is a neat pile of salvaged timber labeled, in large letters, CORVIN\'S. YOU\'RE PAYING FOR THIS.'

k: The Keel Lift's for the Keel-crew only. Ardent's orders.
src: 'The Keel Lift\'s for the Keel-crew only. Ardent\'s orders.'

k: In the brass cradle where Skyreach's Dawnstone should sit, a single silver tuning fork stands upright, humming to itself.
src: 'In the brass cradle where Skyreach\'s Dawnstone should sit, a single silver tuning fork stands upright, humming to itself.'

k: You know that note. You have been carrying it in your pack for weeks.
src: 'You know that note. You have been carrying it in your pack for weeks.'

k: Wreckage
src: 'Wreckage'

k: THE THORNWOOD.nKeeper's grove beyond. Walk softly; the trees are listening.n_(Underneath, newer, in charcoal: CLOSED. THORNS. DO NOT.)_
src: 'THE THORNWOOD.\nKeeper\'s grove beyond. Walk softly; the trees are listening.\n_(Underneath, newer, in charcoal: CLOSED. THORNS. DO NOT.)_'

k: Forage, fletching, and things that fix you. Mostly the first two. Have a look.
src: 'Forage, fletching, and things that fix you. Mostly the first two. Have a look.'

k: The Hollow Log. Hollow log, soft moss, warm stew. Seventy gold, and I'll even let you choose which log.
src: 'The Hollow Log. Hollow log, soft moss, warm stew. Seventy gold, and I\'ll even let you choose which log.'

k: the Hollow Log
src: 'the Hollow Log'

k: The soldiers came a month back. Fifty of them, white and gold, the Hierophant's sun on every shield.
src: 'The soldiers came a month back. Fifty of them, white and gold, the Hierophant\'s sun on every shield.'

k: The big one with the beard didn't even go in. Sat on my woodpile eating our apples while his men carried the Keeper's light out in a box.
src: 'The big one with the beard didn\'t even go in. Sat on my woodpile eating our apples while his men carried the Keeper\'s light out in a box.'

k: Didn't pay for the apples, either.
src: 'Didn\'t pay for the apples, either.'

k: You've seen her? Truly? Is she— is she very old?
src: 'You\'ve seen her? Truly? Is she— is she very old?'

k: Of course she is. I only meant — is she very _kind_? I always imagined she was.
src: 'Of course she is. I only meant — is she very _kind_? I always imagined she was.'

k: I'm writing an epic about Keeper Elowen. Nobody in Rootholm has seen her in thirty years.
src: 'I\'m writing an epic about Keeper Elowen. Nobody in Rootholm has seen her in thirty years.'

k: Some say she is four hundred years old. Some say she has turned into a tree. I have rhymed both possibilities, just in case.
src: 'Some say she is four hundred years old. Some say she has turned into a tree. I have rhymed both possibilities, just in case.'

k: I'm not allowed in the Tangle anymore. Or near the Tangle. Or near anyone who's been near the Tangle.
src: 'I\'m not allowed in the Tangle anymore. Or near the Tangle. Or near anyone who\'s been near the Tangle.'

k: Mum's very thorough.
src: 'Mum\'s very thorough.'

k: I tied a ribbon for Gran on the Memory Tree. A yellow one. She liked yellow.
src: 'I tied a ribbon for Gran on the Memory Tree. A yellow one. She liked yellow.'

k: The pretty lights in the forest weren't her. Ilse said. Ilse says it's all right to miss her anyway.
src: 'The pretty lights in the forest weren\'t her. Ilse said. Ilse says it\'s all right to miss her anyway.'

k: When I'm sixteen I'm going to be a Warden like the big one. Or a Rogue like the small one.
src: 'When I\'m sixteen I\'m going to be a Warden like the big one. Or a Rogue like the small one.'

k: He said I could be both. He said that's allowed now. Is that allowed now?
src: 'He said I could be both. He said that\'s allowed now. Is that allowed now?'

k: The Memory Tree
src: 'The Memory Tree'

k: Fern's crates: bundles of arrows fletched with jay feathers, jars of honey, a sign reading NO HAGGLING, and under it, smaller: (a little haggling).
src: 'Fern\'s crates: bundles of arrows fletched with jay feathers, jars of honey, a sign reading NO HAGGLING, and under it, smaller: (a little haggling).'

k: A statue of a Keeper, so old that her face has worn smooth. Somebody — recently — has put a crown of daisies on her head.
src: 'A statue of a Keeper, so old that her face has worn smooth. Somebody — recently — has put a crown of daisies on her head.'

k: The Lantern
src: 'The Lantern'

k: The Lantern of Thornwood. Roots have climbed it to the gallery; blossom grows inside the lamp-glass.
src: 'The Lantern of Thornwood. Roots have climbed it to the gallery; blossom grows inside the lamp-glass.'

k: The cradle at its heart is empty. A bird has started a nest in it.
src: 'The cradle at its heart is empty. A bird has started a nest in it.'

k: The trees here grow too close to pass. For now.
src: 'The trees here grow too close to pass. For now.'

k: Tide pool
src: 'Tide pool'

k: A worn grave-slab: BRENNA HALLOWAY — FIRST OF US — SHE CUT THE STAIR.
src: 'A worn grave-slab: BRENNA HALLOWAY — FIRST OF US — SHE CUT THE STAIR.'

k: ODA HALLOWAY. SHE HELD THE LIGHT THROUGH THE STORM OF THE SEVENTY BOATS, AND ALL SEVENTY CAME HOME.
src: 'ODA HALLOWAY. SHE HELD THE LIGHT THROUGH THE STORM OF THE SEVENTY BOATS, AND ALL SEVENTY CAME HOME.'

k: IDE HALLOWAY. "SHE SANG FLAT AND NEVER ONCE MISSED A DAWN." Your grandmother. You remember her hands, and her terrible singing.
src: 'IDE HALLOWAY. "SHE SANG FLAT AND NEVER ONCE MISSED A DAWN." Your grandmother. You remember her hands, and her terrible singing.'

k: Lamp
src: 'Lamp'

k: Gate
src: 'Gate'

k: Carving
src: 'Carving'

k: A blank slab, smoothed and ready. Nothing carved on it yet.
src: 'A blank slab, smoothed and ready. Nothing carved on it yet.'

k: A small, newer stone, the letters cut in a careful, narrow hand you know very well: EDRIN — WHO WAS NOT A KEEPER, BUT KEPT US.
src: 'A small, newer stone, the letters cut in a careful, narrow hand you know very well: EDRIN — WHO WAS NOT A KEEPER, BUT KEPT US.'

k: The first Keeper, worn faceless by four hundred years of damp. Fresh candle stubs at her feet. Someone comes down here often. Someone who comes down from the top.
src: 'The first Keeper, worn faceless by four hundred years of damp. Fresh candle stubs at her feet. Someone comes down here often. Someone who comes down from the top.'

k: The great lamp of Lanternfall. Its bed of brass is empty.
src: 'The great lamp of Lanternfall. Its bed of brass is empty.'

k: No time. RUN.
src: 'No time. RUN.'

k: The Lantern door is barred from inside. White light leaks from every crack.
src: 'The Lantern door is barred from inside. White light leaks from every crack.'

k: LANTERNFALL — Westmost Light of Solmere.nChalked beneath, in a soldier's square capitals: HARMONIZATION IN PROGRESS. KEEP TO YOUR HOMES.
src: 'LANTERNFALL — Westmost Light of Solmere.\nChalked beneath, in a soldier\'s square capitals: HARMONIZATION IN PROGRESS. KEEP TO YOUR HOMES.'

k: _(He doesn't look at you. He's looking at the sun.)_
src: '_(He doesn\'t look at you. He\'s looking at the sun.)_'

k: Move along, miss. Please.
src: 'Move along, miss. Please.'

k: That hum. Does it ever stop? It's in my teeth.
src: 'That hum. Does it ever stop? It\'s in my teeth.'

k: I've swept my step eleven times today, Wren.
src: 'I\'ve swept my step eleven times today, Wren.'

k: Every time I look up, the sun's still there. Watching me sweep.
src: 'Every time I look up, the sun\'s still there. Watching me sweep.'

k: Wren! Remember me? Kindling day, right before you — Ranger! I've been practicing every morning.
src: 'Wren! Remember me? Kindling day, right before you — Ranger! I\'ve been practicing every morning.'

k: Everyone's acting like the world's ending. It's just a really long sunset. ...Right?
src: 'Everyone\'s acting like the world\'s ending. It\'s just a really long sunset. ...Right?'

k: One Crest, one life, girl. And one sun, one sky.
src: 'One Crest, one life, girl. And one sun, one sky.'

k: Something up there has forgotten the rules. Eighty years, and I've never seen the sky forget the rules.
src: 'Something up there has forgotten the rules. Eighty years, and I\'ve never seen the sky forget the rules.'

k: My Tamsy's been up all night with folk who say the hum gives them headaches.
src: 'My Tamsy\'s been up all night with folk who say the hum gives them headaches.'

k: She says it isn't a headache. She says it's like remembering something you never did.
src: 'She says it isn\'t a headache. She says it\'s like remembering something you never did.'

k: Tide went out at noon yesterday. Hasn't come back.
src: 'Tide went out at noon yesterday. Hasn\'t come back.'

k: You can walk to the eel rocks now. You can walk to the rocks past the eel rocks. Sea's holding its breath, girl. Long breath.
src: 'You can walk to the eel rocks now. You can walk to the rocks past the eel rocks. Sea\'s holding its breath, girl. Long breath.'
